evidence.paraphrase: People propose investigating the source of the mysterious bell sound by going to examine it.
The king offers a reward for discovering the origin of the bell sound.
evidence.quote:
he who could discover whence the sounds proceeded, should have the
      title of "Universal Bell-ringer," even if it were not really a bell

evidence.paraphrase: A proposed naturalistic explanation attributes the sound to an owl knocking its head in a hollow tree.
evidence.quote:
he said that the sound
      proceeded from a very large owl, in a hollow tree; a sort of learned owl,
      that continually knocked its head against the branches

evidence.paraphrase: A scholarly treatise is written yearly about the supposed owl, yet no real knowledge is gained.
evidence.quote:
wrote yearly a short treatise "On the Owl"; but everybody was just as wise
      as before

evidence.paraphrase: Some children conclude the bell is imaginary and doesn't really exist.
evidence.quote:
In reality the bell does not exist; it is only a
      fancy that people have taken into their heads!

evidence.paraphrase: A child questions whether a sound is the bell and decides it needs investigation.
evidence.quote:
That surely cannot be the bell," said one of the children, lying down and
      listening. "This must be looked to.

evidence.paraphrase: The king's son reasons that the little bell they found could not be the source of the distant sound.
evidence.quote:
the bell was too small and too fine to
      be heard at so great a distance, and besides it was very different tones
      to those that could move a human heart in such a manner

evidence.paraphrase: The king's son resolves to keep searching for the bell no matter how far.
evidence.quote:
I must and will find the bell," said he, "even if I am obliged to go to
      the end of the world.

evidence.paraphrase: Nature is presented as a vast cathedral, contrasting the sought-after church with the natural world.
evidence.quote:
all nature was a vast holy church, in which the trees
      and the buoyant clouds were the pillars, flowers and grass the velvet
      carpeting, and heaven itself the large cupola

evidence.paraphrase: The two boys reunite and finally experience the invisible bell amid nature.
evidence.quote:
They ran towards each other,
      and stood together hand in hand in the vast church of nature and of
      poetry, while over them sounded the invisible holy bell
